name: Letrero ABIERTO / CERRADO
description: Útil para informar si una tienda o lugar está en servicio o no. Impreso por separado y se pegan para formar uno solo.
details:
Tamaño: 29 x 14 cms.   Por ser mayor al tamaño máximo de la cama, dividí en tres partes cada cara:

- La base: lado izquierdo y lado derecho
- El letrero: ABIERTO o CERRADO.
Cuando se imprimen las tres partes de un lado, se entrelazan las que conforman la base y sobre estas se pega la correspondiente a cada letrero Abierto o Cerrado.

Una vez se tengan completos los dos letreros, se pegan entre sí por su parte de atrás.

Incluí tres piezas que sirven de soporte para colocarlo en una puerta o vidrio.  Uno de los soportes se coloca en la parte inferior y los otros uno a cada lado.   Estos permiten que el letrero se pueda fácilmente colocar en una u otra posición dándole la vuelta.

Lo imprimí con PLA y relleno de 10%.   Únicamente los dos soportes laterales requieren utilizar soportes orgánicos que son muy fáciles de retirar.

name: Laacher See Volcano - 3D Terrain Model of Germany's Only Caldera Lake
description:
GThis is a 3D terrain model of the Laacher See - the only water-filled volcanic caldera in Central Europe. Located in the Volcanic Eifel region near Koblenz, Germany, this crater lake was formed around 13,000 years ago during one of the largest volcanic eruptions in European history.


The model captures the distinctive circular caldera basin and surrounding volcanic landscape. You can see the steep crater walls, the lake depression, and how the terrain rises around this geological feature. The eruption that created this caldera was massive - comparable to Mount Pinatubo in 1991 - and its ash deposits can be found all across Europe.


What makes this place special is that it's still volcanically active. CO2 gas bubbles up from the lake floor at the southeastern shore, reminding us that the magma chamber beneath is still there. Geologists consider this one of the most important volcanic sites in Central Europe.


Great for educational purposes, geological visualization, topographic analysis, or just understanding how volcanic calderas actually look. Print it as a physical terrain model to really appreciate the scale and shape of this unique landscape.


The model is based on real elevation data and works well for display, education, or as part of a larger geological collection.

The precision and flexibility of 3D printing enable the creation of intricate structural elements and innovative architectural features, making it a revolutionary solution for modern housing that combines both sustainability and versatility

name: puzzle 3d dell'Italia
description:
Questo modello stampabile in 3D ti permette di costruire una mappa tattile e colorata delle regioni italiane. Un modo divertente ed educativo per imparare la geografia. Perfetto per progetti scolastici, giochi in famiglia o semplicemente per decorare la tua stanza. 

Per realizzare un'Italia magnetica, occorre predisporre ogni regione con delle calamite di dimensioni specifiche. In particolare, tutte le regioni italiane, eccetto la Liguria, sono predisposte per l'uso di calamite di dimensioni 6x3 mm. La Liguria, a causa della sua conformazione particolare, richiede invece calamite più piccole, di dimensioni 3x1 mm.

Per garantire che l'intera mappa d'Italia risulti magnetica, è necessario inserire una lamiera magnetica tra i due strati che compongono la mappa: la cornice e il riquadro delle regioni. Questa lamiera fungerà da base magnetica, permettendo alle calamite delle varie regioni di aderire saldamente e mantenere la loro posizione sulla mappa.

Assicurarsi che la lamiera sia ben fissata tra i due strati per evitare movimenti o disallineamenti delle calamite. Dopo aver montato la lamiera, posizionare le calamite nelle rispettive regioni, tenendo a mente le diverse dimensioni necessarie per la Liguria rispetto alle altre regioni.

name: Ferris Wheel
description:
Based on Fairground attraction, this working model is a ferris wheel approx. 700mm. 
All components are made on an Ender 3v2. -  220x220 bed
The only additions are a small assotrment of m3 set screws and nuts, and a length of 4mm threaded bar. The drive is a tiny standard geared motor powered by a 9 volt (PP3) battery.
Files for the gearbox are included.
I've used string for the drive belt, as it reduces friction on the pullies, as opposed to a rubber belt or 'o' ring (which are too elastic). 
You can email me at 1@cooltogo.co.za if you require geometry layout and file location diagrams and also a short video.
A total of 6 Mb  in  38 files. 
The pods are printed in 2 parts and glued together.
No supports are required.
There is an optional tensioning rod to find the 'sweet spot' of the drive.
Approximately 1 revolution in 45 seconds.
details:
Ender 3v2  using PLA.
Hot end - 210 degrees
Bed - 60 degrees

name: just a pretty house
description:
For the floor and roofs I used supports and only 10% infill to save filament and time. You can use fuzzy skin for the floor.


For both roofs I changed filament to give them the two colors they have, you can see them in the photos.


For the first roof I changed the filament at layer height of 4.40 and for the second roof I did it at layer height of 5.20.

On the first ceiling you will need to use glue to stick an object with the name L roof, you can see it in the photos.

For the brick wall I used 15% infill and brim.

For the walls I used 15% infill and supports, although I don't think they are necessary, but you can use them if you want.

For the pillars I also used brim and 15% infill.

For the smart side panels I recommend printing them upside down for better details except for the one from the attic, use brim and tree supports only for those that are required, you can also use glue if you want to stick them on the walls.

I am including the garage without a door as well and if you can print in multicolor you can put one more color on the door as well if you want.

I designed the house to be printed without needing a multicolor printer, you can chose the colors you want for your house.

I printed everything at 0.2 mm

i used PLA for everything.

name: Puerta de Alcalá in removable blocks for children
description:
The Puerta de Alcalá is one of the best known symbols of Madrid.


The original reason for my design was that my wife wanted a **detachable block version** so that the children at her school (she is a teacher) could assemble and disassemble it, as part of a class on cities.


Some pieces include the pivots to assemble, while others need to be fitted additionally (printed separately).


CONTAINS SMALL PARTS. DO NOT USE WITH CHILDREN UNDER 6 YEARS OF AGE.


It is a design with a medium level of detail (possibly in the future I will make an improvement of the statues, as they have hardly any details).


The size, once assembled, is about 22cm from end to end.


I printed this block version in gray (see photos).





In addition to the block version, I prepared two other versions in two other STL files:


- **a complete one**, to print in one piece (requires a lot of supports).


- **and another one divided in two halves**, its two facades (to be able to print it with less supports), which must be glued with glue. I made a test print in a smaller size, in white color (see photos). It didn't look bad, although logically details are lost.

Whether you're looking to enhance a scale model, create stunning dioramas, or experiment with structural designs, these Pillar Columns provide an authentic touch.

Crafted with precision, our model showcases detailed elements of Doric, Ionic, and Corinthian styles, making it perfect for historical recreations or modern architectural accents. The columns are designed for easy printing on most 3D printers, ensuring a smooth and hassle-free printing experience. Made to be robust yet aesthetically pleasing, they serve as both decorative and load-bearing elements in your designs.

Key Features:
- Accurate representation of classical column styles
- High-resolution detailing for a realistic look
- Compatible with most 3D printers
- Versatile use in architectural models, dioramas, and educational projects
- Easy to print and assemble

Transform your projects with the timeless beauty and strength of our Pillar Columns. Purchase this model today and bring a piece of architectural history to life with the power of 3D printing.

name: NeoClassical GrecoRoman Temple
description:
NeoClassical GrecoRoman Temple

This model intends to be a 3D recreation of a typical Neoclassical scene depicted in both paintings and sculptures. Neoclassicism itself takes inspiration from the Renaissance period, and mostly tends to represent iconic scenes from Greek mythology and their characters.
Neoclassicism (also spelled Neo-classicism) was a Western cultural movement in the decorative and visual arts, literature, theatre, music, and architecture that drew inspiration from the art and culture of classical antiquity. The main Neoclassical movement coincided with the 18th-century Age of Enlightenment, and continued into the early 19th century, laterally competing with Romanticism. In architecture, the style continued throughout the 19th, 20th and up to the 21st century. Neoclassicism is a revival of the many styles and spirit of classic antiquity inspired directly from the classical period.

name: Realistic Grass 3D Model for 3D Printing - STL Format
description:
Realistic Grass 3D Model for 3D Printing - STL Format





Description:





Transform your 3D printing projects with our realistic grass model, designed to offer an authentic touch to your models, dioramas and art projects. This innovative STL model creates exceptionally fine tufts of grass, thanks to a design thought out for upright printing that uses natural filament bridging.





Features:





Format : STL


Dimensions: several sizes available


Complexity: Easy to Medium, ideal for beginners and experienced users alike


Compatibility: compatible with most FDM and SLA 3D printers


Details: high-resolution model with finely detailed blades of grass


Printing: print vertically to exploit natural filament bridging and create distinct blades of grass


Media required: No media required


Printing instructions:





For best results, here are some printing tips:





Recommended nozzle: Use a fine nozzle (0.4mm or less) for precise detail and well-defined blades of grass.


Print speed: Reduce print speed to improve quality and ensure clean bridging between blades of grass.


Print temperature: Adjust the temperature according to the filament used (generally between 190°C and 220°C for PLA).


Recommended materials: PLA, PETG or any other filament compatible with your printer. PLA is often preferred for its ease of use and smooth finish.


Fill parameters: A low fill (10-20%) is sufficient, as the bulk of the model relies on the contours and individual strands.


Applications:

Landscape models: create strikingly realistic countryside scenes, gardens and parks.


Dioramas: Add natural detail to your dioramas for model railways, tabletop games or educational projects.


Art projects : Incorporate natural elements into your artworks, sculptures or installations.


Why choose this model?





Realistic: meticulously designed to mimic the look of natural grass.


Practical: Easy to print without the need for media, with detailed printing tips for optimal results.


Versatile: Suitable for a wide range of projects, from miniature models to large dioramas.


Download our realistic 3D grass model now and bring your creations to life with a touch of authentic nature!

name: Senigallia's Rotonda a Mare 3D Model Reproduction
description:
Experience the beauty of Senigallia's iconic Rotonda a Mare with our stunning 3D model reproduction! This intricately designed replica captures the essence of this historic landmark, allowing you to bring a piece of Italian seaside charm into your home.

Description:
The Rotonda a Mare, located in Senigallia, Italy, is a symbol of the town's rich maritime heritage and vibrant beach culture. Originally built in the early 1930s, this distinctive structure features a circular wooden platform supported by stilts, extending out into the Adriatic Sea. Over the years, it has served as a popular gathering place for locals and tourists alike, offering panoramic views of the sea and coastline.

Our 3D model faithfully recreates the Rotonda's unique architecture and intricate details. The base is divided into four sections, while the upper part consists of three pieces held together by the dome. Each section is designed for easy assembly, allowing you to recreate the Rotonda's iconic silhouette with ease.

In addition, the model features window openings with slots for inserting transparent plastic, providing a realistic portrayal of the Rotonda's distinctive windows.

Measuring approximately 430x440 mm at the base and standing approximately 140 mm tall when assembled, this model is designed to capture the grandeur and beauty of the original monument.

Whether you're a fan of Italian architecture, a history enthusiast, or simply looking for a unique conversation piece, our Rotonda a Mare 3D model is sure to impress. Add a touch of Italian coastal charm to your home or office with this exquisite reproduction.

name: Grand Duchess Charlotte Bridge - Rout Bréck
description:
This 3D model represents the iconic Grand Duchess Charlotte Bridge, locally known as the "Rout Bréck" due to its distinctive red paintwork. Spanning the Alzette River, the bridge serves as a crucial artery linking Avenue John F. Kennedy in Kirchberg to Boulevard Robert Schuman in Limpertsberg. 

It is a vital connection between Luxembourg City's historic center, Ville Haute, and the Kirchberg district, home to numerous European Union institutions. The model captures the bridge's significant structural and aesthetic details, emphasizing its role as a key infrastructure component in Luxembourg City.

Assembling the different parts requires only a little bit of super-glue.
Scale: 1:1420

description:
**READ THE DESCRIPTION FIRST !**
(I have Ender 3 V2, program "Creality Print/Cura")

I haven't been here for a long time but I decided to come back because I missed the Cults3d community.
  I created a Greek-like structure with "water" surrounding it and a bowl to look like a "map/teleporter", it can be use to decorate a room or garden (ABS or PETG).
You can choose the bowl you want, Bowl1-TextPlate, Bowl2 or bowl3-stand if you're unpatient (it's optional extender for bowl1-TextPlate.stl, look at the pic on gallery).

For "Bowl1" you have another option to select a plate with text, i.e. style, (TextPlate from 1-3).This model contains holes as markers to facilitate orientation where the plate should be glued. 

You can also paint that model as you wish.
details:

- PLA/ABS

**recommended nozzle parameter:** 
- 0.2mm  (called "normal")
- 0.16mm (called "dynamic Quality")

Supports:YES (60o-90o or everywhere)

**infill:**
- Bowl: **25%**
- Architecture:**40%**

**Time**:
- MainArchitecture.stl: **5h 41m** (0.16mm) 

**Rotate the bowls2-3 to save time and material  Y:180o or -180o**
- Bowl1-TextPlate.stl: **~3h 20m** (0.2mm, support 60o)

- Bowl3-stand.stl:**6h 25m**(same)
- TextPlate 1-3: **~31min**(0.2mm, support 80o-90o,)

**NOTE**
If one of the models is very tiny, just scale that model by 740% and **AFTER** that, scale to your preferences (if you want to).

name: Maritime Station in Constanta
description:
Entering Constanța Port through the main access gate, you can't help but notice the impressive building of the Maritime Station. Built between 1931 and 1933 according to the plans of architect Gheorghe Brătescu, the Maritime Station was inaugurated on August 15, 1934, on Romanian Navy Day, in the presence of King Carol II. The need to build such an edifice was imposed, at the time, due to the explosive growth of port activity, both for the traffic of goods and for people. Thus, the travelers arriving by water, in Constanța, were to be greeted by the majestic building, which together with the silos built by Eng. Anghel Saligny, represented the pride of the country's largest port.

From the Maritime Station you could go directly by ship to Constantinople, Alexandria, Piraeus, Naples, Marseille or New York or by train to Bucharest.

name: The observatory lighthouse in Sulina
description:
Among the most impressive monuments of the city of Sulina we find the Observatory Lighthouse or the Lighthouse of the European Commission of the Danube. Built in its current form between 1869-1870 by the European Commission of the Danube after the project of the doctor M. Engelhardt under the coordination of Sir Charles A. Hartley, the truncated conical lighthouse has a height of 17.34m.

Currently, the Sulina Lighthouse operates as a museum, among the exhibits the pieces of furniture that belonged to the writer Jean Bart and his family photos, the collection of weapons from the 18th - 20th centuries, medals, documents, maps and photos regarding the activity European Commission of the Danube.

name: Glykon - Decorative Magnet
description:
In the 2nd century AD the cult of the snake Glykon, probably of Macedonian origin, was widespread from the Danube to the Euphrates, this deity being given powers related to fertility and protection against plague. The popularity of the cult is demonstrated by coins with the representation of the snake Glykon minted in the 2nd and 3rd centuries AD in the Roman Empire. The cult lost its followers after the death of its founder, the Greek prophet Alexander of Abonutichus, around 170, although some evidence suggests that it still managed to survive into the 4th century.

The Glykon statue, currently at the Museum of History and Archeology in Constanța, is special in that it is the only representation of this kind discovered so far in the world. The statue was discovered in the spring of 1962, during the modernization works in the area of ​​the old station in Constanța, together with 23 other statues carved in marble representing divinities worshiped in Tomis.

The glykon discovered in Constanța dates back to the 2nd century AD and is masterfully carved from a single block of marble with a side of 66 cm. The deity is represented on a plinth, having the body of a coiled serpent, the head of a woman, the snout of a lamb and the tail of a lion, and if unfolded, would be 4.76 m long.

name: King Carol Lighthouse in Constanta - Decorative Magnet
description:
King Carol Lighthouse in Constanta - Decorative Magnet

The King Charles I Lighthouse located within the Port of Constanța was inaugurated in 1909, taking over the baton from the old Genovese Lighthouse on the Constanţi Beach. Built under the auspices of the first king of Romania after whom it is named, the octagonal lighthouse stands proudly at 21.75m above sea level, representing at the time, one of the most modern constructions in its category. The Charles I lighthouse is mounted on a stone tower facing the sea decorated with the effigy of the king, and on the opposite side with the bust of Roman Emperor Trajan.

name: Hunkiar Mosque in Constanta
description:
Geamia Hunkiar also known as Geamia Aziziye is the oldest Muslim place of worship in Constanța. The construction of the historical monument took place between 1861 and 1869. The window is built in Moorish style, from ancient stone blocks, having a square-shaped main body that houses the prayer hall and a minaret whose height reaches 24 meters.

The Hunkiar window was in danger of being demolished in 1942 due to the damage sustained a year earlier due to the bombing of Constanta by Soviet aviation. In the sixth decade of the last century, the window was restored, but only after 1989 was it returned to the faithful.

name: The old lighthouse in Mangalia
description: Known as the "old lighthouse", this lighthouse was erected in the mid-50s of the last century on the highest point of Mangalia, 30 meters above sea level, and is today one of the main tourist attractions of the city. Renovated a few years ago, the old Mangalia lighthouse at the end of the pier guards the tourist port of Mangalia like an old sea wolf.

name: King Carol Mosque in Constanta
description: King Carol Mosque in Constanta. Historical monument built in 1860.

name: King Carol Lighthouse in Constanta
description: The King Charles I Lighthouse located within the Port of Constanța was inaugurated in 1909, taking over the baton from the old Genovese Lighthouse on the Constanţa Beach. Built under the auspices of the first king of Romania after whom it is named, the octagonal lighthouse stands proudly at 21.75m above sea level, representing at the time, one of the most modern constructions in its category. The Charles I lighthouse is mounted on a stone tower facing the sea decorated with the effigy of the king, and on the opposite side with the bust of Roman Emperor Trajan.

name: The old lighthouse in Sulina
description:
The Old Sulina Lighthouse is mentioned for the first time in an old Ottoman document which says that it was built at the initiative of Beshir Agha in 1745. In 1856 the lighthouse was rebuilt from the foundations by the Ottomans, and between 1869-1870 it was modernized by the European Commission of Danube. Located at the end of the north breakwater of the Sulina Canal, shaped like a circular metal tower raised on a carved stone base, the lighthouse is 13.7m high and operated until 1920 when work began to extend the breakwaters from the mouth of the Sulina Canal.

The old lighthouse in Sulina was used in the 70s for the filming of the Romanian series "Toate pânzele sus!".

name: Genoese Lighthouse in Constanta
description:
Genoese Lighthouse in Constanta

The Genoese lighthouse near the Casino Cliff in Constanța is one of the well-known historical monuments of the city and one of its symbols.

Built from stone blocks carved by the French engineer of Armenian origin, Artin Aslan, between 1858-1860, the 8.75m tall Genovese Lighthouse is shaped like an octagonal prism placed on a rectangular base and is decorated with an elegant cornice with consoles. The Genovese Lighthouse guided ships at sea for over five decades, until its task was taken over by the newly built King Charles I Lighthouse at the end of the pier in Constanța Port.

The Genovese lighthouse was commissioned by the English company "Danube & Black Sea Railway" which also built the Cernavodă-Constanța railway, the first railway in Dobrogea, respectively in the Ottoman Empire of which the province was a part at the time.

name: Lighthouse of Snake Island
description:
Known in Antiquity as Leuke, Leucos or Achilles' Island, Snake Island has been intensely disputed in recent centuries, belonging in turn to the Ottoman Empire, the Russian Empire, Romania and Ukraine.

The first lighthouse on Snake Island was built between 1837-1842 on the island's plateau, approximately 40 m above sea level. After 1877, the maintenance of the lighthouse was ensured by four guardians, a Romanian, a Greek, a Turk and a Bulgarian. The lighthouse was destroyed in 1917, during the First World War, by the German cruiser "Breslau". In 1922, the lighthouse was rebuilt by the European Danube Commission.

In 1947, Snake Island was taken from Romania by the USSR, after its dissolution it returned to Ukraine. A year ago, the lighthouse was destroyed by Russian bombing of the island.

name: Glykon
description:
In the 2nd century AD the cult of the snake Glykon, probably of Macedonian origin, was widespread from the Danube to the Euphrates, this deity being given powers related to fertility and protection against plague. The popularity of the cult is demonstrated by coins with the representation of the snake Glykon minted in the 2nd and 3rd centuries AD in the Roman Empire. The cult lost its followers after the death of its founder, the Greek prophet Alexander of Abonutichus, around 170, although some evidence suggests that it still managed to survive into the 4th century.

The Glykon statue, currently at the Museum of History and Archeology in Constanța, is special in that it is the only representation of this kind discovered so far in the world. The statue was discovered in the spring of 1962, during the modernization works in the area of ​​the old station in Constanța, together with 23 other statues carved in marble representing divinities worshiped in Tomis.

The glykon discovered in Constanța dates back to the 2nd century AD and is masterfully carved from a single block of marble with a side of 66 cm. The deity is represented on a plinth, having the body of a coiled serpent, the head of a woman, the snout of a lamb and the tail of a lion, and if unfolded, would be 4.76 m long.

He is often depicted with an elephant head and a human body, sitting or standing in a relaxed posture. His four arms might hold symbolic objects such as a lotus flower, an axe, a bowl of sweets (modak), and his broken tusk.

Materials: The clock could be made from various materials, including wood, metal, plastic, or a combination of materials. The image of Lord Ganesha might be intricately carved, embossed, or printed onto the clock's surface.

Symbolism: Beyond its practical function as a timekeeping device, a Ganesh Ji clock holds symbolic significance for devotees of Lord Ganesha. It serves as a reminder of his presence and blessings in their lives, as well as a focal point for prayers, meditation, and spiritual contemplation.

Size and Features: Ganesh Ji clocks come in different sizes, ranging from small tabletop versions to larger wall-mounted ones. Some clocks may have additional features such as chimes, LED lights, or musical tunes associated with Hindu devotional songs.

Overall, a Ganesh Ji clock combines the functionality of a timepiece with the spiritual significance of Lord Ganesha, making it both a practical and meaningful addition to any home or sacred space.

name: Chorizo House with Neoclassical Elements
description:
Architectural description:
This facade belongs to an urban “chorizo” house, with a strong sense of symmetry and formal elements of Italian Classicism adapted to the traditional domestic architecture of the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

Notable features:
Vertical tripartite composition, with an axis of symmetry centered on the main entrance, framed by ornamented pilasters

Double-leaf solid wood door with a glazed transom and a wrought-iron grille on a raised platform

Three vertical openings with Majorcan-style shutter-type shutters (dark green), typical of Spanish-American architecture

French balcony-style cast-iron railings at the base level, protecting the main openings

Expressive use of exposed brick as a decorative element, integrated into vertical panels and pilasters

Paris stone-style stucco, in light ochre, with simulated rustication created by horizontal joint lines

Upper finish featuring multiple ornamental cornices and a frieze with horizontal moldings, typical of the Italianate style

Wall decoration on central panels (vertical mirror-shaped brick panels), which could be reminiscent of old signage, artistic stucco, or closed-off ventilation openings

Typological observations:
This facade is reminiscent of homes built between 1890 and 1930, designed for a narrow, deep lot

The elevated entrance, with its staircase and gate, signifies a hierarchical distinction in access

The Majorcan shutters not only provided privacy, but also passive climate control

The use of symmetrical elements and pilasters reflects a desire for a monumental appearance in the homes of the affluent middle class

name: 4ft Vertical Plank Facades in HO Scale
description:
Every HO scale Wall You'll Ever Need!
--------------------------------------
    By Steve Baker
    Renaissance Miniatures.

The goal here is to provide EVERY possible type of wall that
you're ever likely to need!

However, being utterly comprehensive comes at a cost.

The set of all possible wall sections (every possible height,
length, curvature, material, etc) adds up to 1,500 STL files
and several gigabytes of data.

This is FAR beyond maximum download limits.

The surface finishes on them are VERY detailed - aimed to
have sufficient resolution to produce the best POSSIBLE quality
for even the MOST accurate 3D printer.

They are zipped together into 42 ZIP files - each between 60 and
120 Mbytes.

There are currently seven different surfaces modelled:

  * Brick -- A fairly plain, new-ish looking brick.
  * DistressedBrick -- A very old brick wall, which has seen better
    days.
  * DamagedConcrete -- A severely damaged concrete wall with bits
    of rebar showing.
  * Dressed Stone -- Neatly squared off stone blocks.
  * DryStone -- A traditional building style with random
    chunks of stone, piled up to make a strong, lasting wall.
  * DrySlate -- Another traditional style with layers of flat
    slate pieces.
  * VerticalPlank - More of a fence, made with vertical planks.

I have made an STL file with one wall of each type so you can
choose which materials you are interested in.  You can find it
here as: "Wall Samplers".

I recommend you print that on your printer of choice
before downloading vast amounts of data!!

HOW ARE THE ZIP FILES ORGANIZED?
--------------------------------

These models come in two types:  "Wall" and "Facade".

"Facades" have one textured side and one smooth side.  They are very
useful when using these parts to scratch-build larger structures.
You can also lay them onto the smooth side for printing which will
make them print MUCH faster on a resin printer.

"Walls" are textured on both sides with a smooth base so they can
be glued to your baseboard "as is".

They also come in three different heights:
    4 feet, 6 feet and 8 feet.

WHAT IS WITHIN EACH ZIPFILE?
----------------------------

Each ZIP file contains walls of one surface type, either facade
or wall and at one specific height.

So, for example, when you decide you want to enclose a farmyard
with (say) Dry Stone walls - choose "wall" rather than "facade"
and download that specific ZIP file - and you'll have every
possible length/curve/etc that you could possibly need for that
project.

If you plan to use these for scratch building structures, then
you probably want the inside of the wall to be smooth - so in
that case, choose "FACADE" rather than "WALL".

Within each ZIP file, there are hundreds of STL files for different lengths, different curvatures and with either rough or smooth ends.  Smooth ends make it easy to CA glue multiple pieces together.  Rough ends look better at the ends of the wall.

Use the "middle" ones for the middle of a long wall because
they are smooth on both ends.

Use either "left" or "right" pieces for the ends of the wall.

There are also "single" pieces which are textured on both ends
if you just need a very short section.
 
  -- Steve.

name: ottoman clock tower
description:
The Tophane Clock Tower (Turkish: Tophane Saat Kulesi) is a clock tower in Bursa, Turkey. It has six floors and is 33m in height.
The tower currently has a radio clock and is used as a fire lookout station.

There was a different clock tower in the place of the current one, which was destroyed in an unknown date. 
The construction of the current tower began on 2 August 1904 and was finished on 31 August 1905.

name: Circus 3D Model
description:
Circus 3D Model

A full environment model of a circus built onto a stage, this can easilly be converted into a tent.

Details include stage design for performance, lighting rigs and high beam lights, scaffolding for support of various parts of the stage ie. curtain and pyro rigs.

Concept is entirely unique, although the elephants are not included as they are not mine.

Stage includes rope barriers and is designed with a surrounding crowd pit towards the entrance with lighting ready to be customised for night and day.

Full lighting grid at the top of the model, 2 projection screens, pyro cannons and curtains. Materials are as shown.

The Blender file is ready to go in realtime in Eevee or for rendering in Cycles as seen in screenshots.

Polycount is: 541983

Includes Blender file, .fbx and .obj formats.

Scene can be easily optimised for games on certain elements.

Contact me on: thesurgerymusic@gmail.com if you have any issues.

Circus 3D Model by Jonathan Shoesmith.

name: Leaning Tower of Britten Diorama
description:
Here we go!

Make the amazing diorama of Britten's Leaning Tower in Groom (Texas) yourself.

Print all the pieces of the diorama.
To create the handrail perfectly, print it flat on the plate, wait for it to cool and gently detach it from the plate so it doesn't get ruined (just like the ladder).
Heat the plate of your printer to 70° degrees and place the ladder flat, waiting for it to soften.
Once it has become a little soft, take it and wrap it around its template, perhaps fixing it with an elastic band and wait for it to cool and keep its shape.

Apply a thin layer of Primer, then color with Vallejo acrylic colours.

Color the entire base with Bonewhite (cod. 72.034 Vallejo).

Color whit White the Body and the Pump Hose.
With Red and Blue color the text on the Body like in photo.

Take a red color and put just a little of brown and mix to obtain the dark red like in real photos.

Color all the other pieces with this.

Connect the Parts whit Loctite SuperAttack.
Once the paint has dried, apply a light layer of glossy protective clearcoat.

name: World's Largest Pop Bottle Tribute
description:
The Giant Soda Pop Bottle Pop's on Route 66 is another iconic place to stop (Arcadia, Oklahoma).
In 2007 a minimalist 66-foot-tall soda bottle sculpture named "Bubbles," and an accompanying soda-centered roadhouse named "Pops," debuted on Route 66.
They were deigned by Oklahoma City architect Rand Elliott, and the vision of fracking billionaire Aubrey K.

With this my exclusive design that I created by searching for the original designs of the bottle, you can choose different options to recreate your personalized tribute depending on your tastes:

- WHITE BOTTLE (like during the hours of the day with the sun); you'll need only a White filament.

- COLORED BOTTLE (like in the night); you'll need primer and the following Vallejo colors (or similar): Sun Yellow (code 72.006), Orange Fire (code 72.008), Bloody Red (code 72.010), Wartora Purple (code 72.014), Ultramarine Blue (code 72.022), Electric Blue (code 72.023), Dark Green (code 72.028), Goblin Green (code 72.030) and, as usual, a protective transparent for the final step. Remember to paint ONLY the rings, not the internal part!

- GLOW IN THE DARK BOTTLE (for an unique design); you'll need a Glow in the Dark filament.

In addition to all this, you can decide whether to use the normal base or with the LEDs which will allow you to obtain an even more exciting result, so you'll need 2 LEDs and a battery to power them.
If you decide to print the Pop Bottle in white, you can use two red, white, green or blue LEDs and you will get an excellent visual effect.
If, however, you want to make the colored Pop Bottle, consider exclusively the use of cold white LEDs.

For the base, I recommend coloring it with a dark grey, but you can also make it black as you like.

Take a look at all the example photos I have included to better understand the various results you can obtain.

Also keep in mind the material at your disposal.

There are 38 different rings in this project and they must be inserted into the straw in the order indicated by the names (number one is the top one and number 38 is at the bottom of the bottle).
If you intend to color the various rings, you can use a string to thread them all without losing the correct order (look in the photos I posted).

Check out my profile for all the other unique creations made as a tribute to Route 66!!!

Don't forget to share your print, give this project a like and have fun!!!!

name: Caporossello Lighthouse - Realmonte/Agrigento, Italy
description:
The Capo Rossello Lighthouse is located in the municipality of Realmonte, Sicily. It is located at the tip of Capo Rossello, a promontory overlooking the Mediterranean Sea. The lighthouse was built in 1859 and is 40 meters high. The tower is cylindrical and has a white lantern that emits a beam of white light every 10 seconds. The lighthouse is an important landmark for maritime navigation and also offers a breathtaking panoramic view of the Sicilian coast.

The Capo Rossello Lighthouse is also the brightest lighthouse in Sicily.

The Capo Rossello Lighthouse is a popular tourist destination and offers a unique experience for all those visiting Sicily.

This model was created with Tinkercad.
details:
You can try different settings, for this 3D model mine are:

- Material: VOXELAB PLA, white.

- Nozzle Diameter: 0.4mm

- Layer Height: 0.2mm

- Infill: 15% or more

- Supports: Yes.

Important things to know:
- As for the glass, I used a piece cut from a plastic bottle and inserted it into the groove I created in the heart of the lighthouse and on the roof. To prevent it from moving or falling, I recommend using glue.
- The only part of the structure that needs supports is the balcony/protrusion of the lighthouse.
- In order to have a reproduction as faithful as possible to the lighthouse, I went in person to take photos, both from the ground and from the drone.

Check out my other uploads on my profile , you might like them.

Here are some general tips for printing:





*Bed leveling:* Make sure the print bed is leveled properly for even adhesion on all layers.





*Temperature calibration:* Adjust the printer temperature according to the recommendations of the material you are using for optimum results.





*Support check:* Verify that supports and support structures are properly configured to ensure stability during printing. **(This design does not require supports)**.





*Filament check:* Before printing, verify that the filament is free of knots or jams, and that it is correctly inserted into the feed system.





*Moisture control:* For moisture sensitive materials, consider storing filament in a dry place to avoid problems during printing.





*Curing time:* If you are using resin, pay attention to the recommended curing time to ensure proper solidification of the layers.





*Monitoring during printing:* Monitor the print during the first few layers for potential problems and stop the print if settings need to be adjusted.





*Regular maintenance:* Perform regular maintenance on your printer, such as cleaning nozzles and checking connections, to maintain consistent performance.





These tips will help you optimize the printing process, regardless of the type of printer you use.

name: Buddha Design
description:
The Buddha is seated in a classic meditation pose, with legs crossed and hands resting on the lap in a gesture of meditation or enlightenment (Dhyana Mudra). The back is straight, and the overall posture conveys a sense of tranquility and inner peace.
The facial expression is serene and compassionate, with closed eyes and a gentle smile. The forehead may have a symbolic mark, such as the third eye, representing spiritual insight. The ears are elongated, symbolizing the detachment from worldly possessions.
The Buddha is draped in flowing robes that fall naturally around the body, with intricate folds and details. The robes should have a sense of simplicity and elegance, symbolizing renunciation of materialism.
The hair is short or in a tight topknot, with visible spirals or curls. There may be a cranial protuberance (ushnisha) at the top of the head, symbolizing wisdom.
Minimal ornamentation, such as a necklace or simple jewelry, may be included. The focus is on spiritual rather than material wealth.

bottom panel, and auxiliary vectors (SVG, DXF, EPS, AI, PDF) to assist in carving the rails and stiles.

1285 mm x 732mm x 27 mm - 50.6" x 28.8" x 1.06" All-in-One version
1295mm x 732mm x 40mm - 50.98" x 28.8" x 1.575" - Panelized version

This purchase includes:

name: Electric Gates 3D Model
description:
Electric Gates 3D Model – Realistic Automated Gate and Fence Asset

Enhance your architectural visualizations or game environments with this Electric Gates 3D Model by CGHawk. This detailed 3D asset includes electric gates and wall railings, designed for both realistic rendering and real-time use.

Features:

High-Quality Design: Realistic electric gates with wall railings — perfect for architectural visualization, urban scenes, and simulation environments.
